meaning: The number 200,000,000 (two hundred million) is mentioned in Revelation 9:16 as the size of a massive cavalry army in the end times.
description: In Revelation 9:16, John describes a gigantic cavalry army of 200 million released by the river Euphrates to kill one-third of humanity. John himself emphasizes that he heard the number—a phrasing suggesting the size is deliberate and significant. The number symbolizes an overwhelming, almost incomprehensible military force expressing God’s judgment in the last days. Some interpreters read the number literally as a future army, while others see it as a hyperbolic expression of a power so great that it is impossible for humans to resist.

versions.description: In Revelation 9:16, John describes a gigantic cavalry army of 200 million released by the river Euphrates to kill one-third of humanity. The number symbolizes an overwhelming, almost incomprehensible military force and God's judgment in the last days. In Jewish and Christian interpretive tradition, the number has been understood both literally as a future army and symbolically as expressing the power of an invincible divine judgment. Some interpreters see it as a hyperbolic figure representing a strength so great that it is impossible for humans to resist.
versions.reason: [minor] The description is generally good, but the claim about a 'Jewish interpretive tradition' is somewhat imprecise – the figure of 200 million comes specifically from Revelation (a Christian text), and there is little specific Jewish tradition tied to this exact number. The wording should be adjusted for accuracy.; [minor] It may be helpful to move details about various interpretive traditions (literal vs. symbolic) into a footnote, so that the description flows better as coherent text.; [minor] The footnotes array is empty. It would have been natural to include at least one footnote on the Greek expression 'dis myriades myriadon' (two myriads of myriads), which is the original wording in the base text, as well as one on the role of the Euphrates in a biblical context.

footnotes.text: The Greek expression in the original text is 'δισμυριάδες μυριάδων' (dis myriades myriadōn), which means 'twice ten thousand times ten thousand'. The myriad (10,000) was the largest number concept in ancient Greek language, and a double myriad of myriads thus expresses an almost incomprehensible quantity.

The river Euphrates held great symbolic and strategic significance in biblical tradition. It formed the northeastern boundary of the promised land (Gen 15:18) and was historically the border river between the Roman Empire and the Parthian Empire. The fact that the army is released specifically at the Euphrates links it to ideas of invasion from the east—a threat well known in the ancient world.

In Christian interpretive history, the number has been linked to everything from literal future military forces to demonic armies. Church Father Victorinus of Petovium (died c. 304) interpreted the cavalry army allegorically, while modern dispensationalists have occasionally attempted to connect the number to actual military capabilities.
